surface_mechanism_description: The growth process involves a two-step mechanism where the first step is a rapid reaction with the bare substrate and the second step is a slower process that may involve reorganisation on the surface to allow for a denser packing of the precursors or a slow decomposition. The reaction rate of H2O with the adsorbed In-complex is low and saturation is not reached even after 7 s of pulsing. A clear mass increase is observed when water is introduced, whereas one would expect a decrease in mass as the acac-ligands are replaced by less massive OH-ligands, the reason for this is unclear. For growth with O3 a mass reduction is observed as the oxidant is introduced, however, the reaction rate is also here slow and it is difficult to assess the time frame for saturation.
evidence: Investigations using QCM on the different growth processes resulted in the signals presented in Fig. 1. These show a two-step growth process when In(acac)3 is adsorbed on the substrate. The first step involves a rapid reaction with the bare substrate and lasts less than 1 s, the next step is a slower process that may involve reorganisation on the surface to allow for a denser packing of the precursors or a slow decomposition. However, we did not observe any film when only In(acac)3 was pulsed as a test. The investigation also shows that the reaction rate of H2O with the adsorbed In-complex is low and that saturation is not reached even after 7 s of pulsing. One peculiarity is that a clear mass increase is observed when water is introduced, whereas one would expect a decrease in mass as the acac-ligands are replaced by less massive OH-ligands, the reason for this is unclear. For growth with O3 a mass reduction is observed as the oxidant is introduced, however, the reaction rate is also here slow and it is difficult to assess the time frame for saturation.
